newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity up sharply on weather, outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity up sharply on weather, outages.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rose sharply Wednesday on forecasts of warm weather in the U.S. Southwest and several unexpected generation outages, industry sources said.

"There are a couple of short-term outages in the West and that seems to be the main factor (in the price rise)," said one Houston-based futures trader, adding "we've got over 5,000 megawatts in outages right now that are unplanned."

In the U.S. West, Salt River Project (SRP) said its 750 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at its Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Arizona, tripped off line early Tuesday, but was ramping back towards full power late Tuesday.
Moreover, all three Navajo units had been operating at half load over the past few days due to mild weather and weak demand for electricity, SRP said.

Pacific Gas & Electric Co said its Moss Landing natural gas-fired plant in Monterey, Calif., tripped off line late Monday, and was expected to resume operation Wednesday afternoon. The Moss Landing station on the central California coast has two units with a total capacity of 1,500 MW.
Also, the 750 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired plant in Nevada had been expected to return to service Tuesday following a Saturday shutdown for maintenance.
Startup of a 185 MW unit 1 at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico was delayed to early Wednesday due to a boiler tube leak.
Also, the 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state and 1,087 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in southern California were scheduled to resume output by next week.

As of 1205 EDT, July Palo Verde (PV) was trading up $2.39 per megawatt hour (MWh) at $32.60 following exchange in a range of $31.20-33.10, while August was up $1.68 at $33.60 after trades at $32.80-33.70 per MWh.
July California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up $1.11 at $20.80 following exchanges in a range of $20.25-21.00, while August was up 77 cents at $23.55 after trades at $23.10-23.75 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1125 EDT an estimated total of 121 COB and 284 PV contracts had traded.
Futures have also taken some strength in recent days from concern over reduced Northwest power supplies to southern California this summer.

A Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) committee on Tuesday introduced a proposal to derate the Pacific Intertie transmission system from July 1-30 to 6,300 MW from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
The plan still requires the approval of the WSCC board.

Separately, the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) did not offer any firm power for delivery during peak demand hours on Thursday, compared with recent offers of 200 megawatts a day, the agency said Wednesday.
Previously, BPA had offered peak firm power for delivery today at $16.50 per MWh in the Northwest and at $17.50 at COB.
As of 1205 EDT, July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up two cents at $2.179 per million British thermal units.
